description: Machine-derived ratchet baseline for the web/API PostgreSQL application-parity migration through task quick-sort workflow parity, L18 AI execution and memory control-plane persistence, and L19 webhook configuration/delivery/log parity, L12c finance end-user web/API parity, runtime observability parity, merged L09 finance parity, L05 task-read parity, L07 task-write parity, L13 notification-web parity, L14 external-agent parity, L15 project-hierarchy parity, L16 ideation-workspace parity, L17 derived-analytics parity, L11 connector-management parity, L12a connector-domain parity, L12b finance connector/operator parity, L08a triage web persistence, and L08b triage native persistence. Recomputed and enforced by web-persistence-baseline.test.ts via computeWebPersistenceGraph (tests/architecture/web-persistence-graph.ts). Every count below is a ceiling: a later layer may only decrease it (or leave it unchanged), never increase it. Every taint-side path array is an allowlist ceiling (recomputed sets must be subsets of the baseline set); cleanRoutes is a floor (recomputed set must be a superset). LEGACY_RAW_SQLITE_IMPORTS and other documented fail-closed exceptions are migration targets counted as taint here, not grandfathered exclusions.

provenance.tierAAlgorithm: Ported line-for-line from the approved planning session file files/tiers.mjs (staticSources/dynamicSources seeded strictly from static-vs-dynamic import kind; Tier A = static-only backward reachability). This is the canonical source for tierARoutes/tierBRoutes/cleanRoutes/taintedLibA/taintedApiHelpers/totalMigrationUnits; it reproduced the plan's committed 266/221/39/6/123/6/350 baseline at introduction and now records only verified ratchet reductions.
provenance.directDbNamespaceAlgorithm: Faithfully ported from the planning session file files/reach2.mjs's directDb check (route file's own resolved, static import edge has an original specifier matching /^@\/db(\/|$)/). Reproduces the plan's committed 144 exactly against this commit. This is a structural/namespace metric, independent of Tier A/B membership -- see knownArchivedGeneratorDefect.
provenance.directTaintSourceAlgorithm: New metric introduced by this layer (L01): the exact partition of tierARoutes into routes with an edge whose TARGET is literally one of staticSources (directTaintSourceRoutes) vs. routes tainted only transitively (transitiveOnlyTaintSourceRoutes). By construction, directTaintSourceRoutes.length + transitiveOnlyTaintSourceRoutes.length === tierARoutes.length always holds. Do not conflate with the plan's committed 144/79 figures (see knownArchivedGeneratorDefect for the exact reconciliation).

knownArchivedGeneratorDefect.symptom: reach2.mjs's seedTaints(f) seeds a taint set from every driver-matching specifier in a file's COMBINED external-import set (static + dynamic + require), without gating on the includeDynamic parameter passed to computeReachable(). Its 'static-only' reachability pass therefore also seeds from files whose ONLY driver reference is a dynamic import()/require() -- incorrectly treating them as immediate, zero-hop static taint sources. This inflates reach2.mjs's own staticTainted route count to 223, a strict superset of the correct tiers.mjs Tier A count (221).

affectedRoutes.reason: Only reaches a taint source via src/lib/connectors/github-issues/backup-verifier.ts (a dynamic-only source per tiers.mjs); correctly Tier B, not Tier A. Was miscounted by reach2.mjs as staticTainted=true AND directDb=true (the directDb=true part is independently valid: this route does have its own static @/db/persistence/github-recovery-values import, but that submodule does not itself reach any taint source).

Only reaches a taint source transitively via .../backup-verifier.ts (dynamic-only); correctly Tier B, not Tier A. Was miscounted by reach2.mjs as staticTainted=true with directDb=false, landing in the archived transitive-only=79 bucket.

knownArchivedGeneratorDefect.reconciliation: Plan.md's committed '79 transitive-only' = reach2.mjs's buggy staticTainted count (223) minus its directDb count (144) = 79; this number is preserved here verbatim as a historical/archived figure but is NOT reproduced as a ratchet field because it inherits the defect above. It is exactly one more than the true Tier-A-exclusive figure (78 = transitiveOnlyTaintSourceRoutes.length), because exactly one of the two defect-affected routes (sync/retained/resolve) falls in that bucket. Plan.md's committed '144 direct' is NOT defective on its own (directDb is a clean, static, file-local check unaffected by the seed bug) and is reproduced exactly by directDbNamespaceRoutes; it happens to include one route (github-bulk-transfer) that is not itself Tier A, which is why tierARoutes.length (221) does not equal directDbNamespaceRoutes.length (144) + transitiveOnlyTaintSourceRoutes.length (78) (221 vs 222); the correct Tier-A partition uses directTaintSourceRoutes (143 = tierARoutes intersect directDbNamespaceRoutes) instead.

finalTarget.note: Zero normal production web/API SQLite evaluation under PostgreSQL, per plan.md's final target, with only a minimal, audited, fail-closed exception list (throwing before any SQLite import/effect) surviving.

invariants: directDbNamespaceRoutes is NOT guaranteed to be a subset of tierARoutes (see knownArchivedGeneratorDefect)

layerUpdates.summary: Web/API PostgreSQL parity: seed/demo fail-closed audit fix, entity-link cross-backend parity, and a fully clean settings/mode route migration.
changes: src/lib/seed-api.ts and src/lib/seed.ts exit taintedLibA and staticSources (better-sqlite3 import became import type, erased at build time; the real handle is now obtained via a lazy `await import('@/db')` inside getDb(), which fails closed under MC_DATABASE_BACKEND=postgres before that import ever runs).

src/app/api/settings/mode/route.ts exits tierARoutes AND tierBRoutes entirely (was directTaintSourceRoutes; a transitional design briefly moved it to tierBRoutes via call-site dynamic imports, but the final design removes even that). The route now imports only the pure, backend-neutral `@/lib/settings/mode-route-services` registry (zero import edges -- static or dynamic -- to `@/db`, `@/lib/seed-api`, or `@/lib/triage/lifecycle`; the one value-level import it needs, `RelativeReminderTimezoneRepository`, is `import type`-only). Both the PATCH handler's timezone repository and the POST handler's three demo-only commands (reset-demo/clear-data/clear-triage-samples) are resolved through this registry's plain get accessors. The concrete SQLite and PostgreSQL implementations are constructed and registered once, at server startup, by `initializeRuntimeDatabase()` in src/db/runtime.ts -- the same, already-established composition root used for `CorePersistenceRepositories` -- so the route module itself never touches SQLite/PostgreSQL machinery at all, at import time or call time. For PostgreSQL, the timezone repository gets a real adapter (createPostgresRelativeReminderTimezoneRepository); the three demo commands have no PostgreSQL equivalent and reject with the same 'SQLite-only' error text already used by seed-api.ts/triage/lifecycle.ts, constructed inline in the PostgreSQL branch without importing either SQLite-only module.

src/lib/tasks/relative-reminder-timezone-runtime.ts (a transitional lazy dynamic-import resolver) was deleted; its role is now split between the pure registry (`@/lib/settings/mode-route-services`, owned by this layer, not `src/lib/tasks/` which is owned by a later layer) and the composition-root wiring in `src/db/runtime.ts`.

src/lib/triage/lifecycle.ts and src/lib/triage/shared.ts are unchanged in tier (still Tier A/tainted): their normal, non-demo functions (updateTriageItemThumbnail, hardDeleteTriageItem, hardDeleteTriageItems, purgeDismissedItems, ensureSeedData, and others) are explicitly NOT migrated by L02 and are NOT given a fail-closed guard merely because they share a module with clearTriageSampleData (the one genuine seed/demo exception in that file); they remain an explicit later-layer target, not narrowed L02 taint.

The notification entity-linking repository files (src/db/persistence/notification-entity-linking.ts and its SQLite/Postgres adapters) gained an ASCII-fold suffix-match parity fix and a JSON-string-type guard; neither file is on the tainted-graph census path (they are called from webhook/worker code already migrated by prior layers), so this change does not affect any count in this baseline.

layerUpdates.summary: Web/API PostgreSQL parity: the Ideation workspace domain now selects its backend through the composed worker persistence facade instead of a hardcoded SQLite composition root, retiring the last tainted shared API helper.
changes: src/lib/persistence/sqlite-runtime.ts is deleted. It was a SQLite-only composition root that existed solely for ideation workspaces and had exactly one consumer; the SQLite adapter is now composed in src/db/persistence/sqlite-worker-runtime.ts alongside every other backend-selected repository.

WorkerPersistenceRepositories gains a top-level `ideationWorkspaces` slot. It is not nested under an existing slot (as L15 nested projectAutomation.hierarchy) because graph_workspaces and graph_workspace_versions share no rows and no serialization namespace with any other worker surface.

src/lib/graph-workspace/service.ts exits taintedLibA: it now holds an async repository resolver over getWorkerPersistenceRepositories() rather than a constructed SQLite repository, so it evaluates no driver at import time.

All five src/app/api/ideation/workspaces/** routes exit tierARoutes and enter cleanRoutes with no source change: none of them ever imported the @/db namespace, so the entire decrement is transitive (directTaintSourceRoutes and directDbNamespaceRoutes are unchanged at 124 and 125).
src/app/api/ideation/workspaces/route-errors.ts exits taintedApiHelpers, which reaches the declared finalTarget of 0 and is the first ratchet field in the programme to be fully retired.

src/db/postgres/repositories/ideation-workspace-repository.ts is added. No schema migration was required: graph_workspaces and graph_workspace_versions, both unique indexes, both plain indexes, and the cascade foreign key already ship in drizzle/postgres/0000.

Both adapters share shouldCheckpointIdeationRevision from the neutral contract module, and both order the library by (archived, updated_at DESC, ASCII-folded name, id). The trailing id tiebreaker defines an order that was previously unspecified in SQLite; PostgreSQL reproduces SQLite COLLATE NOCASE with ASCII-only translate(...) COLLATE "C" rather than a locale-aware lower(name).

PostgreSQL deleteArchived runs inside one FOR UPDATE transaction where SQLite reads then deletes non-transactionally. Single-threaded behaviour is identical; PostgreSQL is intentionally stronger under concurrency. duplicate deliberately stays non-atomic in both backends.

layerUpdates.summary: Web/API PostgreSQL parity: the read-only derived-analytics surfaces (dashboard/reset KPIs, the /insights query layer, cumulative flow, and the tag/word insight services) now select their backend through the composed worker persistence facade.
changes: WorkerPersistenceRepositories gains a top-level `analytics` slot holding five sub-repositories (kpis, insights, flow, tagInsights, wordInsights). It is top-level because these read models share no rows and no serialization namespace with any other worker surface, and one slot rather than five because they are registered atomically: a backend supports every analytics surface or none.

src/lib/stats/index.ts, src/lib/stats/insights.ts, src/lib/stats/flow-query.ts, src/lib/tag-insights/service.ts, and src/lib/word-insights/service.ts exit taintedLibA. Each now holds an async repository resolver over getWorkerPersistenceRepositories() and evaluates no driver at import time. Every exported signature, JavaScript reducer, date and timezone computation, clamp, and error string is unchanged.

All six owned routes exit tierARoutes with no source change: none of them ever imported the @/db namespace, so the entire decrement is transitive and directTaintSourceRoutes (124) and directDbNamespaceRoutes (125) are unchanged.

src/app/api/insights/observations/route.ts reclassifies from Tier A to Tier B rather than becoming clean. Its residual reach is a deferred import() of @/lib/ai/config-resolver inside src/lib/stats/observations.ts, which is owned by the held AI provider layer and was deliberately not touched.

No schema migration was required. The layer is read-only: no column, table, constraint, default, or index changed, and every table it reads (tasks, task_projects, task_tags, tags, hub_projects, project_phases, project_phase_items, task_history_events, routines, routine_completions, notifications, triage_items, my_day_items, focus_items, connector_configs) already ships in drizzle/postgres.

Neither backend opens a transaction, takes a row lock, or raises the isolation level. The multi-query composites (computeKpis and the eleven-way insights summary fan-out) were non-atomic under SQLite and stay non-atomic under PostgreSQL; a snapshot would give callers a consistency guarantee they do not have today. The per-project and per-day query loops are preserved deliberately rather than collapsed.

PostgreSQL reproduces SQLite julianday() instant comparison with a guarded CASE using pg_input_is_valid, so unparsable text yields NULL (row excluded) instead of raising, and offsetless text is read as UTC via ::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' rather than the session TimeZone. Every text ORDER BY, window ORDER BY, and row_number() partition order is pinned with COLLATE "C" to reproduce SQLite BINARY byte ordering, and the synthetic-tag prefix scan uses ASCII-only translate(...) rather than a locale-aware lower(). Explicit tiebreakers were added in both adapters for the source breakdown, active/visible projects, delivery filter options, delivery records, active routines, and the unbounded routine-completion reads, defining an order SQLite previously left unspecified.

The PostgreSQL adapter reproduces the Drizzle notificationNeedsAttention() predicate, not the sibling NOTIFICATION_NEEDS_ATTENTION_SQL text constant, whose digest clause excludes rows with a NULL level. notifications.level is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'fyi' in both schemas so no live row diverges; the shared contract pins the distinction anyway.

src/db/task-history.ts is unchanged and keeps both of its consumers. The SQLite adapter calls getTaskTransitionsInRange directly, so no read model is split across two owners and a later burn-report layer inherits it as is.
